scene: Below deck in the dark hold by lantern light, water spraying in jets through two cracks between the planks of the sloop's side. The Carpenter (broad, bald man of about fifty, short gray beard, rolled sleeves, brown canvas apron full of tools) presses one mitten hand flat on a spraying seam and hammers a wad of oakum into the other with a wooden mallet, cheeks puffed, eyes bulging, ankle-deep in water. Behind him, Tom (navy waistcoat, no hat) bails frantically with his wooden bucket, and the Captain (black tricorn, full brown beard, burgundy long coat) peers down the ladder from the bright hatch above, calling down. Tension: the whole ship depends on one exhausted man.

On a captured merchant ship's deck in bright sunlight, the Carpenter tugs a heavy wooden ship's pump free with both arms, wincing, while the merchant ship's own young carpenter (thin, red-haired, gray shirt, worn tool bag) clings to the other end with a desperate face and points at water already sloshing on the deck. The Quartermaster (dark-brown wavy hair, light stubble, white shirt, dark-brown waistcoat) stands behind with his ledger, raising one eyebrow. A spare wooden spar is tucked under the Carpenter's arm. Tension: one carpenter robbing another of the thing that keeps his ship afloat.
